notes: **Presenter:** Joshua. One person, one list, in video order.
**Before recording anything:** nothing in this video uses Qube, Claude, Codex or a terminal on screen. It's Joshua talking plus one hand-drawn-style table. Four assets, that's all.

**The six numbers** (ours, typical estimates, Mark Oct 27) must match the script exactly: Python (from scratch) 300 hrs · Pine Script 100 hrs · QuantConnect 150 hrs · Excel 60 hrs · ChatGPT 5 min · Qube 15 min.

open.text: Nothing blocks the shoot. If you want different times in the table, change the cell in A1 and the matching spoken word in the script (Pine Script's 100 hrs and Qube's 15 min are on screen only, never said).

rows.how: 1. Phone vertical (9:16), eye level, office lights on, lock focus and exposure. 2. Frame close: face and shoulders fill the frame, a mic in front of him at chin height and slightly to one side (any podcast mic on a stand or boom arm; it's a prop, the phone records the sound). 3. Leave space above his head: the editor crops him to the top 37% of the screen (1080×710). 4. Record the hook twice, clean. 5. Then the whole script, lines 1–16, in **one take**, calm, no pauses between lines, no cuts. If he stumbles, start the take again from line 1. 6. Look at the lens, with a glance down now and then, as if reading the table.

1. Open https://excalidraw.com in Chrome. Menu → Canvas background → white #FFFFFF. 2. Text tool, font "Hand-drawn", colour black #1E1E1E, size L. 3. Type the header row on one line, two columns: left `Tool`, right `Time`. Draw a thin grey #9AA3AE line under it. 4. Under the line, small text (size S), grey #9AA3AE, left-aligned: `Our estimates`. 5. Left column, one name per row, size L, same row spacing every row: `Python (from scratch)` · `Pine Script` · `QuantConnect` · `Excel` · `ChatGPT` · `Qube`. 6. Right column, right-aligned, size L, same rows: `300 hrs` · `100 hrs` · `150 hrs` · `60 hrs` · `5 min` · `15 min`. 7. On the ChatGPT row, right after `5 min`, small text (size S) in red #EF4444: `untested`. On the Qube row, right after `15 min`, small text (size S) in green #22C55E: `tested`. (Same row, not under it, so every row is the same height and the box moves the same distance each time.) 8. Rectangle tool: black #000000 fill, solid, sharp corners, no stroke. Draw it over the whole Time column, from just under the `Our estimates` line down well past the Qube row (it must be taller than the column so its bottom is always off-screen, like the original). Make it a little wider than `15 min tested`. 9. Zoom so the table fills a 1080×1210 area (portrait). Save the file as `J029_A1_table.excalidraw`. **CHECK: read the six numbers back against the list at the top of this sheet: 300 hrs, 100 hrs, 150 hrs, 60 hrs, 5 min, 15 min. Units in every cell.** **CHECK: the box hides every number, the red `untested` and the green `tested` before recording starts.**

1. A1 open in Chrome, full screen, no tabs, bookmarks or toolbars showing (hide the Excalidraw toolbar: View mode, or crop it in the edit). 2. Start a screen recording (QuickTime → File → New Screen Recording, whole screen). 3. Click the black box once so the move cursor (four arrows) shows on it. Hold 5s. 4. Drag the box straight down by exactly one row, so `300 hrs` shows. Hold 5s. 5. Repeat, one row at a time, holding 5s after each: `100 hrs`, `150 hrs`, `60 hrs`, `5 min untested`, then drag it off the last row so `15 min tested` shows. Hold 5s on the full table. 6. Stop. 7. In the edit: keep it one continuous shot (no cuts); stretch each hold with a freeze frame so each drag lands on its spoken word (`J029-2-EDIT.md`). **CHECK: each drag uncovers exactly one row, in this order: Python, Pine Script, QuantConnect, Excel, ChatGPT, Qube.** **CHECK: no row shows a number before its drag (watch the box edges).**

lines.text: So how long does it take to crack every quant trading industry role?
For research, we have around 12,000 hours, 9,000 of those being hardcore math.
Hardware engineer, think FPGA, low latency.
Not a lot of people go for this.
It's not on anybody's radar, and that's why it pays so much, and it's probably not as competitive as you think.
Dev, around 1,200 hours.
We can cut this down by 300 to 400 hours with getcracked.io.
More with our upcoming placement accelerator.
Then we have DevOps.
Think infrastructure as code, chef, deployments, CICD, etc.
800 hours, trade-offs, the easiest one, trade reconciliation, slippage, settlements, really things nobody wants to do, 500 hours, lowest bar to entry.
And lastly, we have something that you'll compete against other people fiercely in.
This is statistics, probability, EV, trading games, almost everything that you can think of that you need to execute and trade well.
This is going to take 1,500 hours.
